name: Nuclear plant safety
value: ZNPP power cut 8 Nov; worker killed 9 Nov
summary: Zaporizhzhia lost off-site power on 8 Nov and a worker was killed by a drone on 9 Nov; IAEA warns of winter grid risk
state: Zaporizhzhia lost its 330kV off-site power line on 8 Nov and ran on emergency diesel generators until the connection was restored, the plant's 27th loss of off-site power of the conflict according to the IAEA (Interfax-Ukraine). A plant worker was killed in a drone attack on 9 Nov, the second in under two weeks (United24), and on 15 Nov IAEA Director General Grossi warned that grid risks may increase in winter (APA). Searches on 20 Nov found no damage to safety-critical systems, INES level 2 event or radiological release.
for_you: There is no radiological risk to the public. National nuclear regulators and the IAEA publish official updates on plant safety in Ukraine.
rubric_hit: Loss of all off-site power on 8 Nov and IAEA warning of deteriorating grid safety meet Watch

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
